newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures rebound, March/May dominates.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures rebound, March/May dominates.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures reversed their earlier weak trend to finish sharply higher on Friday helped by New York and ahead of March's first notice day on Monday.

Traders said the climb gained momentum as the market absorbed forecasts of Brazilian 1997/98 coffee crop by private crop watcher Leon Yallouz. One trader said Yallouz put the crop at 27.5 million 60-kg bags.
"That's supposed to be the number, 27.5 million," he said. "I think we have been down for the last two days because of Yallouz and now it's out, I think the market can rally a bit."
Yallouz said earlier on Friday that the report was released on Thursday but the information had only been made available to private clients.

The forecast by Yallouz, the former U.S. Department of Agriculture crop forecaster, compares with Brazilian trade estimate of 23 million. Brazilian producers are expecting a harvest of around 20 million.
London's May contract finished Friday at $1,597 a tonne, a $25 rise on the day, after failing to hold at the day's peak at $1,600.
March, which enters the month-long delivery period on Monday, reaped $48 at $1,590, thus narrowing the March/May spread to just $7.
The active March/May switches were earlier seen traded at $28-$35
"Many people were tidying up positions ahead of Monday's first notice day," said one. There was brisk price-fixing from both roasters and origin sellers.
The uncovered positions on March fell further to just 2,581 lots by the close of business on Thursday, down 992 from a day earlier.
Volume on the market reached 10,815 lots, with March and May accounting for some 7,700 of the turnover.
